name: Self Employment and Entrepreneurship Development
objectives: Develop different types of skills (psychomotor and affective domain) so that students acquire the competencies/programme outcomes through properly designed and implemented practicals/exercises.
ref: Learning websites: http://www.ediindia.org ; http://niesbud.nic.in/docs/SelfEmploymentBook.pdf ; http://smallb.in/ ; http://www.msme.gov.in/ ; http://nimsme.org/ ; http://www.nsic.co.in/ ; http://iie.nic.in/ ; http://msme.gov.in/guidelines_pmegp_24092008.pdf
rule: 6 practical exercises, approx 28 hours in total
note: a) It is compulsory to prepare a log book of exercises; each exercise must be recorded in the logbook, checked and duly dated and signed by the teacher. The practical marks depend on continuous and timely evaluation of exercises. b) Term work report must not include any photocopy, printed manual/pages, litho etc.; it must be hand written / hand drawn by the student only. c) For practical ESE, students are assessed for competencies achieved.

exps.title: 1 Preparatory activity: a) List various types of industries. b) Narrate need of self employment. c) Anticipate importance of entrepreneurship development.
exps.aim: Approx 2 hours. List industries, explain the need for self-employment and the importance of entrepreneurship development.
exps.formula: Industry types: primary, secondary, tertiary; also micro, small, medium, large scale
viva: Who is an entrepreneur?
A person who starts and manages a venture, taking risk to earn profit.
Why is self-employment needed?
It creates jobs, uses local skills and reduces dependence on salaried jobs.

exps.title: 2 Creativeness and innovativeness: a) List at least ten uses of an assigned mechanical feature based item/product (pen, gear, mouse, notebook, chair, table, fan, mobile, bicycle etc.) other than pre-defined. b) List at least ten innovations of an assigned process, product or service. c) List at least ten engineering products which have passed through innovativeness.
exps.aim: Approx 4 hours. Group of 5-6 students: think out of the box to list ten alternate uses, ten innovations, and ten innovated engineering products.
exps.formula: Creativity = new ideas; innovation = new ideas put to use
viva: Difference between creativity and innovation?
Creativity generates ideas; innovation implements them to create value.
Give an innovated product example.
The mobile phone evolving into a smartphone.

exps.title: 3 Identification of self-employment areas: a) Group of 5-6 students. b) List at least five mechanical feature based areas with self-employment potential; select one promising area. c) Develop market survey format. d) Perform market survey nearby the institute. e) Describe the outcome and narrate the experience. f) Attach photographs of group conducting the survey (compulsory).
exps.aim: Approx 4 hours. Choose a promising area, design a survey format, conduct a market survey and report the outcome with photographs.
exps.formula: Sample survey: define objective → questionnaire → collect data → analyse → conclude
viva: Why do a market survey?
To learn customer needs, demand and competition before starting a venture.
What goes in a survey format?
Respondent details, product/service questions, price and demand questions.

exps.title: 4 Visit report: a) Visit any one near institute: industries/financial institutions/bank/training institute/hotel/farming/agribusiness etc. b) Prepare the visit report including: i. brief history of organization; ii. type and details of product/services/support/assistance being given; iii. any other information useful to be a self-employer or entrepreneur; iv. brochures/technical literature collected from agencies.
exps.aim: Approx 4 hours. Visit one organisation and write a visit report with history, products/services, useful information and brochures.
exps.formula: Report structure: introduction, organisation profile, observations, learning, attachments
viva: What is included in a visit report?
History, products/services, useful entrepreneur information and collected brochures.
Name a financial institution helping entrepreneurs.
SIDBI, NSIC, or nationalised banks under PMEGP/MUDRA.

exps.title: 5 Preparing project feasibility report of assigned product: a) Teacher assigns one product (physical or service based) to the group of 5-6 students. b) Prepare project feasibility report (technical and financial), specifically including capacity requirement calculations and project set up planning details; present to the whole batch.
exps.aim: Approx 8 hours. Prepare and present a technical and financial feasibility report for the assigned product.
exps.formula: Break-even quantity = Fixed cost / (Selling price per unit − Variable cost per unit); Payback = Investment / annual net cash flow
viva: What is a feasibility report?
A study of whether a project is technically and financially viable.
Define break-even point.
The output at which total revenue equals total cost.

exps.title: 6 Case analysis and presentations: teacher assigns one case of a successful entrepreneur and one case of a failed entrepreneur to the group of 5-6 students; discuss, analyze and present to the whole batch; prepare the report on analysis. Case may be put up with printed pages but analysis has to be hand written.
exps.aim: Approx 6 hours. Analyse one successful and one failed entrepreneur case, present and submit a handwritten analysis.
exps.formula: Compare: idea, funding, market, management, risk handling, reasons for success/failure
viva: Common causes of business failure?
Poor planning, lack of funds, weak market understanding, poor management.
Qualities of a successful entrepreneur?
Risk taking, innovation, leadership, persistence and planning.
